Tic Tac Toe is a game for two players, X and O, who take turns marking the spaces in a 3×3 grid. The player who succeeds in placing three of their marks in a horizontal, vertical, or diagonal row wins the game.

## How to play

- Click on a square to place your mark.
- The first player to get three of their marks in a row wins the game.
- If the game ends in a draw, the game is a tie.

## Rules

- The game is played on a 3×3 grid.
- Each player takes turns placing their mark (X or O) in one of the empty squares on the grid.
- The first player to get three of their marks in a row (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) wins the game.
- If the game ends in a draw (no player has three marks in a row), the game is a tie.

## Strategy

- Try to block your opponent from getting three marks in a row.
- Look for opportunities to get three marks in a row yourself.

In the write-through policy, when data is written to the cache, it is also written to the main memory. This ensures that the main memory and cache are always consistent, but can result in slower write performance.

### Write-back

In the write-back policy, when data is written to the cache, it is not immediately written to the main memory. Instead, the cache keeps track of which data has been modified. Periodically, the modified data is written back to the main memory. This can improve write performance, but requires extra management to ensure main memory and cache consistency.

### Write-allocate

In the write-allocate policy, when a write miss occurs, a block is allocated in the cache, and the data is written to it. This allows future reads to be served faster, but increases cache pollution.
